text:
John Tavares comes back Saturday against Montreal in a new spot: left wing. The New York Times reported the move, and Jim Hiller confirmed the return (as posted by The Leafs Nation), which also relayed Auston Matthews saying Tavares has been the best player on the ice at practice. He hasn't played since October 15.

What he brings hasn't changed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.1 scoring chances per 60 from the home plate in front of the net last season, 98th percentile among forwards, and he scored 31 goals. His seven games this season produced seven points, four on the power play, though at 5v5 Toronto got only 30% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. Seven games is nothing to judge on, and our projection still has him at 47 to 71 points the rest of the way. The wing asks less of him in his own end and lets him live where he's always done his damage, around the net. For a 36-year-old with 525 career goals before this season, that might be exactly the right job.
headline: Tavares returns, now on the left wing
